correctness.rationale: Equations (4.6a)–(4.6b) give \(\mu_1\) and \(\mu_2\) explicitly. Setting the selected reciprocal parameter equal to one, squaring once, and restoring the sign of the radical gives the unique finite root \(\alpha_c=(2\beta-\sqrt2(|\gamma|^2+4))/(\sqrt2\beta-4)\) for \(\beta\ne2\sqrt2\). The sign calculation selects \(\mu_1\) below \(2\sqrt2\) and \(\mu_2\) above it; the derivative is positive, so the source's left-hand approach indeed has \(\mu_j>1\). The exact difference from the printed center is nonzero for \(|\gamma|>0\). The singular line is handled separately.

value.rationale: The corrected parameter is the center of a published spectral-transition asymptotic, not an arbitrary invariant. This materially changes where the theorem's asymptotic regime is located without requiring any claim beyond the model's own transition mechanism.
